tagline: Real-time collaborative data exploration, querying, and visualization for teams.
killer_feature: The "Live Collaborative Query Playground" where multiple users simultaneously write SQL, see instant results, and drag-and-drop visualizations onto a shared, real-time dashboard.

architecture.frontend: Next.js (React) with Tailwind CSS and Shadcn UI components (generated via v0.app). Why: Next.js provides a robust framework for rapid development, server-side rendering (SSR) for performance, and API routes for backend integration. v0.app accelerates UI development by generating high-quality, production-ready React components, drastically reducing design and coding time. Tailwind CSS ensures consistent styling and easy customization.
architecture.backend: Node.js (Express.js or Fastify) with WebSocket server (Socket.IO). Why: Node.js is excellent for building fast, scalable APIs and integrates seamlessly with Next.js. Express/Fastify provides a minimal, unopinionated framework. Socket.IO simplifies real-time bidirectional communication for collaborative features, handling connection management and fallbacks.
architecture.database: AWS Aurora DSQL (Serverless v2). Why: Mandatory sponsor tech. Its serverless nature means no infrastructure to manage, scaling automatically, and pay-per-use, perfect for a hackathon. It supports standard SQL, making it versatile for various data types.
architecture.ai_integration: Basic SQL Query Autocomplete & Schema Suggestion. Why: Leveraging the connected Aurora DSQL schema, the backend can provide real-time suggestions for table names, column names, and common SQL keywords as users type in the query playground. This enhances user experience and reduces query errors, demonstrating a practical AI/smart feature without complex ML models, feasible within 48 hours for a solo dev.
architecture.deployment: Vercel for Next.js frontend and API routes. Why: Mandatory sponsor tech. Vercel offers seamless Git integration, automatic deployments, serverless functions for API routes, and global CDN, ensuring fast and reliable access with minimal setup (under 5 minutes for the main app). The lightweight Node.js WebSocket server will be deployed separately on a minimal cloud instance (e.g., AWS EC2 free tier or Render/Fly.io free tier) with a simple `git push` deployment, aiming for quick setup.

must_have: Node.js (for backend API and WebSocket server)
nice_to_have: React Query (for data fetching and caching)
Recharts/Nivo (for advanced data visualizations beyond tables)
Monaco Editor (for advanced code editing experience in query playground)
avoid: GraphQL: Adds too much complexity for a 48-hour solo project. REST APIs are sufficient.
Complex authentication providers (e.g., Auth0, Clerk): Stick to simple email/password or mock authentication for speed.
Microservices architecture: Monolithic Next.js app with API routes and a single Node.js WS server is faster to build.
Custom CSS frameworks: Tailwind CSS and v0.app/Shadcn UI are sufficient for rapid styling.

mvp_scope.hour_0_4: Project setup: Next.js app, Tailwind CSS, Vercel deployment config. Basic authentication (mock user login/session management for collaboration). Vercel deployment of an empty Next.js app. AWS Aurora DSQL instance provisioning and initial table creation (e.g., `users`, `queries`, `dashboards`). AWS S3 bucket creation for CSV uploads. Basic UI components (login, dashboard layout) generated via v0.app.
mvp_scope.hour_4_12: Data Ingestion: CSV upload to S3, then a serverless function to parse and insert into Aurora DSQL (simple table creation based on CSV headers). Aurora DSQL Query Execution: Backend API endpoint to receive SQL query, execute against Aurora DSQL, and return results. Basic Query Playground UI: Textarea for query, button to execute, display results in a simple HTML table. Initial real-time setup: Basic WebSocket server running, client connects.
mvp_scope.hour_12_24: Collaborative Query Editor: Integrate a simple text editor (e.g., `react-textarea-autosize` or a basic `contenteditable` div) with WebSocket-based real-time synchronization for query text. Real-time Query Execution: When one user executes a query, results update for all collaborators in the same session. Query Versioning (basic): Store query history in Aurora DSQL, allow loading previous versions. AI Integration (Autocomplete): Implement backend logic to fetch Aurora DSQL schema and provide basic table/column name suggestions to the frontend editor.
mvp_scope.hour_24_36: Dashboard Builder (MVP): Drag-and-drop interface (e.g., `react-grid-layout` or simple CSS grid) for placing query result tables. Real-time Dashboard Sync: Changes to dashboard layout/content by one user are reflected instantly for others via WebSockets. Basic Visualization: Allow switching between table view and a *single* simple chart type (e.g., bar chart using a basic HTML canvas or SVG, or a very simple Recharts component if time permits) for query results. User Management: Basic "room" or "session" creation for collaborative workspaces.
mvp_scope.hour_36_48: Refinement & Polish: UI/UX improvements, error handling, loading states. Bug Fixing: Address critical bugs. Demo Script Practice: Rehearse the 60-second pitch. Video Recording: Create a compelling demo video showcasing killer features. Documentation & Submission: Prepare README, deployment instructions, and submit.

key_screens: Login/Workspace Selection: Simple, inviting entry point.
Live Query Playground: Centralized editor, results panel, schema explorer, and collaboration indicators.
Collaborative Dashboard: Grid layout with draggable query result widgets, real-time updates.
ux_design.wow_moment: Two users simultaneously typing in the query editor, seeing each other's cursors and text, then one executes the query, and the results *and* a new visualization instantly appear on a shared dashboard for both, all in real-time.

demo_script: Hello judges! Meet QueryForge, the real-time collaborative data workbench. Small teams struggle with scattered data and siloed analysis. Our solution? A unified platform for instant insights. Watch this: My teammate and I are simultaneously querying our AWS Aurora DSQL instance in the 'Live Query Playground.' See our cursors? I'm adding a `GROUP BY` clause, and boom! Instant results update for both of us. Now, I'll drag these results onto our shared dashboard, transforming them into a bar chart. My teammate sees it instantly! We've used AWS Aurora DSQL for flexible data, Vercel for blazing-fast deployment, and v0.app for rapid UI. QueryForge empowers teams to explore, visualize, and collaborate on data like never before. Thank you!
antifragile_features: Implement client-side retry logic with exponential backoff for API calls. Display clear error messages to the user (e.g., "Query failed, please try again"). Cache last successful query results locally to prevent complete data loss on temporary backend issues.

If real-time WebSocket collaboration fails, fall back to a "save and refresh" model where users explicitly save their queries/dashboard changes, and others can manually refresh to see updates. The core query execution and visualization would still function, just without the instant collaboration.

judging_alignment.innovation: Real-time multi-user collaborative query editing and dashboard building is a novel approach for accessible data exploration, especially with diverse data sources and rapid visualization. The integration of v0.app for UI generation significantly innovates the development process itself.
judging_alignment.technical: Demonstrates robust real-time architecture using WebSockets, efficient data handling with AWS S3 and Aurora DSQL, and a scalable deployment on Vercel. The AI-powered query autocomplete showcases intelligent system design. Handling concurrent user interactions and data synchronization is technically challenging and impressive.
judging_alignment.impact: Empowers small teams, startups, and non-profits to democratize data analysis, reducing reliance on expensive tools or complex infrastructure. It fosters better team collaboration and accelerates data-driven decision-making, leading to tangible business and operational improvements.
judging_alignment.presentation: A live, interactive demo showcasing two users collaborating in real-time will be highly engaging. The clear problem/solution statement, focus on sponsor tech, and a concise "wow moment" will make the pitch memorable and impactful.

do_not: Spend more than 1 hour on UI design from scratch; leverage v0.app and Shadcn UI heavily.
Implement complex user roles/permissions; stick to a simple "collaborator" model.
Build custom charting libraries; use a pre-built component or a very basic HTML/SVG rendering.
Over-engineer the database schema; keep it simple and focused on query/dashboard storage.
Try to connect to more than one external API; focus on CSV and Aurora DSQL.
Get bogged down in advanced error handling or edge cases; focus on the happy path for the demo.
Spend time on unit/integration tests; manual testing for critical paths is sufficient for a hackathon.
